english: my heart was in my mouth
also: my heart was in my throat

terms.gloss: my breath was in my nose: I was terrified
terms.comment: Traupman glosses it “my breath was in my nose”. Not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections, so Traupman is the only evidence here.

sources: Lewis & Short: anima · Lewis & Short: nasus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
